message.content:
The sky appears blue because of how sunlight interacts with the gases in Earth’s atmosphere. Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made up of all the colors of the rainbow. Each color travels as a wave of a different length. Red light has long waves, while blue light has short waves.

When sunlight enters the atmosphere, it collides with tiny molecules of air. These molecules scatter the light in all directions. However, they scatter the shorter, blue waves much more effectively than the longer, red waves. This phenomenon is known as Rayleigh scattering.

Because blue light is scattered so widely across the sky, it reaches our eyes from every direction, making the sky look blue. If the atmosphere were thicker or thinner, the sky might appear a different color. For example, during sunrise or sunset, sunlight travels through more of the atmosphere, scattering away most of the blue light and leaving the reds and oranges to dominate the view.
